image_description: A vintage grey typewriter with black round keys. The image focuses on the keyboard area, specifically highlighting the long, horizontal key at the bottom center (the space bar). There is a sheet of paper with text inserted in the carriage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is elongated but does not span the 'full width' of the keyboard; it is flanked by the keyboard frame/casing on both sides. It spans the central typing area, not the entire device width.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is significantly longer than the round type keys, visually appearing to be about 6-8 times the diameter of a single key, which satisfies the 'dramatically greater' criteria even if not exactly 10x.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is flat or slightly concave.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar appears as a smooth, slightly curved (concave) plastic strip, consistent with typewriter design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside and internal mechanical stabilizer bars are completely occluded by the top-down viewing angle and the keycap itself.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label is typically blank with no printed character.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar surface is solid black with no visible letters, symbols, or icons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Positioned centrally between modifier keys on the bottom row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: It is located at the bottom center of the key arrangement. While vintage typewriters don't have 'modifier keys' in the modern PC sense, it is centrally positioned between the edges of the typing block.
The key exhibits a smooth, non-glossy finish typical of vintage plastic or bakelite.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Typically white, black, or gray to match keyboard color scheme.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The key is black, matching the other type keys.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Part of a standard computer or typewriter keyboard.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly integrated into a typewriter keyboard assembly.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the paper is illegible and distorted, resembling AI-generated pseudo-text rather than clear typography. Characters merge and lack consistent baseline alignment.
The round keys have a uniform, slightly 'waxy' or melted appearance with inconsistent specular highlights, lacking the crisp edges and distinct material separation seen in real macro photography.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the keyboard frame
artifact_observations.reasoning: The pink tag/label on the right seems to float or merge awkwardly with the grey casing, and the edge of the typewriter body softens unnaturally into the background.

To assess the overall realism, lighting consistency, and texture quality of the vintage typewriter rendering.
To rigorously analyze the gibberish text on the paper, which is a common AI artifact indicator.
To check for merging or bleeding between the individual round keys and the base plate.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of text on the paper
Geometric regularity of the round keys
Boundary sharpness between the space bar and adjacent keys
Physical plausibility of the typewriter mechanics
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the paper; AI often fails to render coherent paragraphs. Also, verify if the 'space bar' is structurally distinct from the chassis or if it blends in due to generation errors. The checkpoint regarding 'full width' was marked false because it doesn't span the *entire* device width, only the key block—ensure this distinction is maintained in the final score.
